steps: Read the policy head and exact configuration Source, then prepare only supported changes.
Submit guarded intent with an exact Connection and follow the Command to reconciled evidence.
useCase.intendedResult: A narrow provider configuration intent can be reviewed without overwriting captured policy contexts.

preconditions: The policy must have a verified native binding, suitable expectedSource and authorized provider scope.
pitfalls: Unconfigured components remain optional; unsupported components or generic clearing cannot be invented.
A policy change may alter current applicability, but historical policy snapshots and posture remain unchanged.
operations.historicalInterpretation: Earlier UpdatePolicy maps to the explicit native configuration command. The initial subset preserves typed native component/description/sharing semantics while detachment or component clearing remains deferred.

operations.purpose: Admit supported changes to a verified native Resilience Hub service profile.

useCase.title: Enable native dependency discovery for a service
useCase.scenario: Checkout has an established native profile and the team wants to enable dependency discovery through the authorized provider access path.
useCase.whenToUse: When the intent concerns supported provider configuration rather than canonical catalog metadata.
steps: Read the Service head and suitable exact native Source evidence.
Submit the desired discovery setting or other supported changes with expectedVersion, expectedSource and Connection, then inspect command/readback.
useCase.intendedResult: The provider request is tracked separately from observed discovery state and local service membership.

preconditions: The Service must have a verified native binding; connection scope and source representation must match the native object.
pitfalls: Desired discovery state is not evidence that discovery has completed.
Creation, deletion, association replacement, permissions, report configuration and unsupported clearing remain outside this initial command.
operations.historicalInterpretation: The earlier native UpdateService maps here for description, Regions, direct policy attachment and desired discovery. Local UpdateService owns the canonical catalog.

operations.purpose: Edit local explanatory and estimation values owned by a Recommendation.

useCase.title: Add an implementation estimate to a captured suggestion
useCase.scenario: An engineer has sized a recommendation and wants to record effort, cost basis and confidence before prioritization.
useCase.whenToUse: When enriching the captured suggestion with local planning information.
steps: Read the current Recommendation and verify its exact source identity.
Submit title, effort, estimate or note under Recommendation.expectedVersion, using explicit allowed clearFields when needed.
useCase.intendedResult: The same Recommendation receives a new version containing its local enrichment.

preconditions: The service/finding/recommendation ownership chain and current Recommendation version must match.
pitfalls: An estimate is distinct from native assessment execution cost and does not prove remediation.
Assignment, completion and verification belong to WorkItem; enrichment has no separate version clock or workflow.
operations.historicalInterpretation: The prior enrichment capability is retained while concurrency belongs to Recommendation itself and operator workflow is centralized in WorkItem.

operations.purpose: Read a native DevOps workspace representation within the application workspace.

useCase.title: Check the native investigation scope
useCase.scenario: The operator is preparing to inspect investigations and needs the retained native workspace identity and associations.
useCase.whenToUse: When selecting or auditing the native scope used by DevOps operations.
steps: Read the AgentSpace head for navigation, or the exact version pinned by a command.
Inspect identity and selectedObservation before selecting a compatible Connection.
useCase.intendedResult: The native DevOps scope is explicit without confusing it with application tenancy.

preconditions: The AgentSpace and its source evidence must be currently authorized.
pitfalls: AgentSpace is not Workspace and cannot select another application tenant.
A retained association is evidence, not a substitute for current dispatch authority.

operations.purpose: Discover the native DevOps workspace scopes retained within the authenticated application workspace.

useCase.title: Choose the investigation workspace for checkout
useCase.scenario: Several native DevOps spaces are represented, and the operator must choose the one associated with the intended workload.
useCase.whenToUse: When navigating retained native workspace scope before opening tasks or executions.
steps: Traverse the visible AgentSpace list.
Inspect the selected space’s identity, associations and evidence before proceeding.
useCase.intendedResult: The operator can choose a clearly scoped native workspace.

preconditions: Current read permission applies to each returned AgentSpace.
pitfalls: The operation does not provision or switch the application Workspace.
A local list does not prove complete native workspace discovery or grant execution permission.

operations.purpose: Read a retained native INVESTIGATION task and its observed execution memberships.

useCase.title: Understand the investigation linked from an incident
useCase.scenario: An incident review links an Investigation. The responder needs its native task state and the executions actually associated with it.
useCase.whenToUse: When examining one investigation task in its AgentSpace.
steps: Provide agentSpaceId and investigationId, choosing an exact version for a review citation.
Inspect the task observation, execution pointer and membership evidence before opening executions.
useCase.intendedResult: The task and its execution relationships remain explicit and evidence-based.

preconditions: The Investigation must belong to the supplied AgentSpace and its retained evidence must be readable.
pitfalls: Investigation is a canonical projection of a native task, not a claim that a native GetInvestigation API exists.
A task pointer or task state alone does not prove an execution result.

operations.purpose: Browse retained native INVESTIGATION tasks for one AgentSpace.

useCase.title: Review the investigation queue in the correct native scope
useCase.scenario: The lead needs the retained investigations for the selected DevOps workspace before opening a particular task.
useCase.whenToUse: When navigating investigations after establishing AgentSpace scope.
steps: List investigations under agentSpaceId and traverse the local publication.
Open selected tasks and inspect their execution membership and evidence.
useCase.intendedResult: The lead can navigate investigations without merging tasks from different native spaces.

preconditions: The caller must have current access to the AgentSpace and returned investigations.
pitfalls: The list contains retained task representations, not a guarantee of a live native task queue.
Task completion and execution outcomes remain separate observations.

operations.purpose: Read one native DevOps execution under its AgentSpace owner.

useCase.title: Inspect an execution referenced by multiple tasks
useCase.scenario: A task links an execution that originated elsewhere in the same AgentSpace. The analyst needs the execution itself without inventing a single parent investigation.
useCase.whenToUse: When resolving an execution identity from a task membership, chat or evidence reference.
steps: Provide agentSpaceId and executionId, with version when following exact retained evidence.
Inspect rawExecutionStatus, parentExecutionIdentity and selectedObservation before opening the journal.
useCase.intendedResult: The execution can be reviewed independently of any one task’s membership.

preconditions: The execution must belong to the supplied AgentSpace.
pitfalls: An investigation foreign key is not required or inferred.
A native status does not replace journal evidence or prove that a requested tool action succeeded.

operations.purpose: Find native executions within an AgentSpace, optionally through explicit investigation-membership evidence.

useCase.title: Inspect the executions associated with an investigation
useCase.scenario: An investigation has several observed execution links, and the analyst needs the matching executions without assuming exclusive ownership.
useCase.whenToUse: When navigating an AgentSpace’s executions or an investigation’s recorded memberships.
steps: List with agentSpaceId and, if useful, investigationId.
Read each returned execution and inspect the supporting membership evidence from the investigation.
useCase.intendedResult: Shared or referenced executions remain navigable without duplicating their identities.

preconditions: The investigation filter must refer to an authorized investigation in the same AgentSpace.
pitfalls: The filter uses observed TaskExecutionMembership; it does not turn the investigation into the execution owner.
An execution created elsewhere in the same space can validly appear through a retained task link.

operations.purpose: Read a retained native execution-journal envelope and its exact arbitrary content source.

useCase.title: Verify a claimed investigation conclusion
useCase.scenario: A summary cites a journal record as evidence for a possible root cause. The reviewer needs the original record type and retained content.
useCase.whenToUse: When inspecting a specific cited journal item rather than trusting an extracted summary.
steps: Supply AgentSpace, Execution and JournalRecord identities with an exact version when cited.
Inspect recordType and selectedSource, preserving the distinction between raw text and extracted relationships.
useCase.intendedResult: The reviewer can check the actual journal evidence behind an interpretation.

preconditions: The complete ownership chain and source content must be currently authorized.
pitfalls: Journal content is arbitrary JSON; a universal root-cause payload schema is not assumed.
A textual mention of another object does not itself create a verified graph relationship.

operations.purpose: Enumerate retained journal records belonging to a particular native execution.

useCase.title: Review the evidence produced during an investigation execution
useCase.scenario: The analyst wants the execution’s retained journal material before comparing observations and conclusions.
useCase.whenToUse: When discovering journal evidence after selecting an execution.
steps: List records under the AgentSpace and Execution parents.
Inspect relevant records and their sources, using native evidence fields to understand chronology and relationships.
useCase.intendedResult: The execution’s journal envelopes remain visible with their native type and provenance.

preconditions: The Execution must belong to the supplied AgentSpace; every returned record must be authorized.
pitfalls: The API’s ordinary list order is canonical identity order, not a guarantee of native chronological order.
Do not convert arbitrary text mentions into graph links or treat every record as a conclusion.

operations.purpose: Inspect a retained validated approval request, its exact action digest and decision/resume references.

useCase.title: Review the exact action awaiting a decision
useCase.scenario: An execution presents a proposed tool action. The approver needs the authenticated request context and exact scope before deciding.
useCase.whenToUse: When evaluating a known approval request in its execution context.
steps: Read the request under its AgentSpace and Execution, retaining the current version and requestSource.
Inspect the exact action digest and supporting request context before admitting a decision.
useCase.intendedResult: The approver reviews a concrete action scope rather than inferred approval text.

preconditions: The approval request must belong to the supplied execution and have retained validated context.
pitfalls: A waiting task, Markdown button or guessed tool name is insufficient approval evidence.
Decision and resume are distinct commands; neither proves actual tool success.

operations.purpose: Find validated retained approval-request contexts within a native execution.

useCase.title: Surface decisions that need operator review
useCase.scenario: An execution may contain approval requests, and the operator needs the retained validated requests available for review.
useCase.whenToUse: When discovering approval contexts after opening an execution.
steps: List under the correct AgentSpace and Execution.
Inspect each candidate request’s exact content and current state before offering a decision action.
useCase.intendedResult: The interface can expose evidence-backed approval contexts without fabricating provider APIs.

preconditions: The owning execution and each complete request context must be authorized.
pitfalls: This is a consolidated retained-data list, not a native Get/ListApproval API.
A pending task state alone must not create a synthetic ApprovalRequest.

operations.purpose: Read an Asset representation with its selected native version, exact source and file references.

useCase.title: Open the investigation artifact cited in a review
useCase.scenario: A review cites an asset version containing an investigation report. The reviewer needs exactly those files, even if later native asset content exists.
useCase.whenToUse: When following an asset citation or inspecting its current retained representation.
steps: Request the cited Asset version within its AgentSpace.
Inspect nativeVersion, source and exact files, applying current access checks to artifact content.
useCase.intendedResult: The cited asset content remains reproducible through the ordinary entity version contract.

preconditions: The asset must belong to the AgentSpace; retained file access must be currently authorized and available.
pitfalls: nativeVersion is provider metadata, not a substitute for Asset.version.
There is no nested versions collection or separate AssetVersion resource; unavailable exact files never fall back to newer ones.

operations.purpose: Discover retained native assets within an AgentSpace.

useCase.title: Find the investigation report asset
useCase.scenario: The reviewer knows the native workspace but needs to locate the report asset before opening its exact retained content.
useCase.whenToUse: When browsing assets before choosing a particular representation.
steps: List assets for the AgentSpace and inspect candidate names, types and native-version metadata.
Read the selected asset or enumerate its entity history for a historical citation.
useCase.intendedResult: Assets remain discoverable without embedding their entire application history in every row.

preconditions: The AgentSpace and each returned Asset must be within current access scope.
pitfalls: The list returns one selected head per asset identity, not every native or application version.
A matching asset name alone does not identify the exact files cited by an older review.

operations.purpose: Admit creation of a native backlog task with taskType=INVESTIGATION in a verified AgentSpace.

useCase.title: Request investigation of a service degradation
useCase.scenario: Checkout has qualified degradation evidence and the operator wants a native investigation task with a clear title, priority and context.
useCase.whenToUse: When intentionally creating a new native investigation task.
steps: Read the AgentSpace head and select an exact authorized Connection.
Submit title, priority and optional description under the AgentSpace expectedVersion, then follow the durable Command.
useCase.intendedResult: The creation intent and later reconciled Investigation identity can be reviewed separately from execution progress.

preconditions: The AgentSpace and connection scope must be valid; current authority is rechecked before dispatch.
pitfalls: The native operation is CreateBacklogTask, not a native API called StartInvestigation.
A task creation receipt does not prove that an execution began or that a result was produced.

operations.purpose: Admit a decision for one exact validated native approval action.

useCase.title: Approve a reviewed single-use action
useCase.scenario: An approver has inspected a concrete requested action and decides to allow that exact scope once.
useCase.whenToUse: Only when the complete authenticated approval context and action digest are available for review.
steps: Read the current ApprovalRequest and its exact requestSource/actionDigest.
Submit APPROVED with singleUse=true, expectedVersion, exact connection and a clientToken; inspect the decision Command before any resume.
useCase.intendedResult: The decision has a durable receipt bound to the reviewed action scope.

preconditions: The request, source and digest must match; the first release supports exact observed scope and single use only.
pitfalls: REJECTED omits singleUse and native pattern/TTL fields; a successful rejection is a successful decision command.
UpdateApprovalAction has no modeled native idempotency token. A lost response is OUTCOME_UNKNOWN and local replay must not blindly repeat it.
Decision does not resume execution or prove that the tool ran.

operations.purpose: Admit the native approval-action resume message using a validated request and a definitively successful matching decision.

useCase.title: Continue an execution after a recorded decision
useCase.scenario: The approval decision has reconciled successfully. The operator now needs to submit the corresponding resume context without changing the approved scope.
useCase.whenToUse: After a matching decision Command has an exact SUCCEEDED representation and the retained execution context is still valid.
steps: Read the current Execution and pin the validated ApprovalRequest and the successful decision Command version.
Submit ResumeExecution under the Execution expectedVersion and follow the new Command, stream evidence and execution observations.
useCase.intendedResult: Resume submission remains separately observable from decision, credential use and actual tool outcome.

preconditions: The supplied decisionCommand must be the exact successful representation for this request; current authorization and validated interrupt/tool context are required.
pitfalls: An ACCEPTED decision version is insufficient even if the command’s current head later succeeds.
SendMessage has no modeled native idempotency token. A disconnected stream is not permission to resend blindly.
The caller cannot substitute tool or interrupt IDs, and stream completion does not prove tool success.

operations.purpose: Create the first DRAFT representation of a workflow scenario with a typed authoring definition.

useCase.title: Author a checkout resilience exercise
useCase.scenario: An author wants a reusable exercise containing an authorized fault step, an explicit workload criterion and a bounded finalizer.
useCase.whenToUse: When introducing a new scenario identity for review and later publication.
steps: Provide the scenario name and authoring definition with declared inputs, steps and bindings.
Create the draft with a clientToken, then inspect it before publication.
useCase.intendedResult: Scenario version 1 exists in DRAFT state and remains separate from executable publication.

preconditions: The caller needs scenario-authoring authority and the definition must satisfy the authoring schema.
pitfalls: The author cannot set trusted locks, digest, publication state, version or server timestamps.
Creation does not execute a workflow or make the draft admissible to StartRun.
operations.historicalInterpretation: The earlier workflow CreateScenario created metadata separately from revision publication. Consolidation creates a typed draft as an ordinary Scenario representation and keeps trusted compilation publication-owned.

operations.purpose: Read a Scenario’s draft, published or archived representation through one exact-version contract.

useCase.title: Review the published program used by a completed Run
useCase.scenario: A Run pins published Scenario version 2 while version 3 is a draft. The reviewer needs the compiled program and locks used by that Run.
useCase.whenToUse: When inspecting current authoring state or resolving an exact execution definition.
steps: Pass the scenarioId and the Run’s exact scenario version.
Inspect state, definition, publication facts and trusted operation locks retained on that representation.
useCase.intendedResult: The executed program remains unambiguous despite subsequent editing.

preconditions: The Scenario and its retained artifacts must be currently authorized and available.
pitfalls: Omitting version may return a DRAFT head; that is not the program selected by a historical Run.
A native operation registry is not exposed here. A published Scenario shows its resolved locks, not every executable adapter alias.
operations.historicalInterpretation: The prior GetScenarioRevision resolves through GetScenario(version). The older ListOperations concern is narrowed to the locks of an exact publication; general adapter-registry discovery remains later work.

operations.purpose: Browse retained Scenario heads, optionally by their current lifecycle state.

useCase.title: Choose a published exercise for a new run
useCase.scenario: The operator wants to find scenarios whose current heads are published before choosing a specific program version.
useCase.whenToUse: When navigating the scenario catalog or separating draft authoring from published offerings.
steps: List scenarios with the desired state filter.
Inspect the selected Scenario and explicitly pin the intended PUBLISHED version before admission.
useCase.intendedResult: The catalog supports discovery while execution remains tied to an exact publication.

preconditions: The caller must have current access to each returned scenario and any required retained content.
pitfalls: state filters the selected current head, not every historical representation.
A later DRAFT head can coexist with an earlier executable PUBLISHED version; use history for that deliberate selection.
operations.historicalInterpretation: The earlier workflow list is adapted from resource-oriented HTTP to RPC pagination while the v2 lifecycle uses ordinary Scenario versions.

operations.purpose: Publish the next DRAFT version of a Scenario after a guarded authoring edit.

useCase.title: Revise a criterion without changing an already admitted run
useCase.scenario: The error threshold in a published checkout exercise needs review. Existing runs must keep their original program.
useCase.whenToUse: When editing a draft or deliberately reopening a published/archived scenario for authoring.
steps: Read the current Scenario and prepare the authoring definition.
Submit expectedVersion and the intended edits; reopening a PUBLISHED or ARCHIVED head requires an explicit definition.
useCase.intendedResult: A new DRAFT version is created under the same scenarioId while prior publications remain retained.

preconditions: expectedVersion must match the current head; a reopened non-draft needs an explicit authoring definition.
pitfalls: The new draft is not executable and cannot retarget existing Runs.
Omitted draft fields preserve values, but locked published content is not implicitly treated as an editable definition.
operations.historicalInterpretation: Earlier HTTP PATCH and If-Match become closed RPC fields with expectedVersion. Separate revision publication is replaced by guarded draft editing followed by PublishScenario.

operations.purpose: Compile the current draft and create the next PUBLISHED Scenario version with trusted immutable locks.

useCase.title: Publish a reviewed resilience exercise
useCase.scenario: The draft’s criteria, dependencies and finalizers have been reviewed, and the team wants an exact program that can be admitted reproducibly.
useCase.whenToUse: After authoring is complete and before starting runs from the definition.
steps: Read the current DRAFT and submit its expectedVersion with a clientToken.
Inspect the PUBLISHED result, including resolved operation/schema locks and digest, before using its exact reference.
useCase.intendedResult: Publication fixes the validated program and its implementation references under one Scenario version.

preconditions: Compilation must validate DAGs, typed bindings, capability checks, required criteria, finalizers and fixed language/reducer semantics.
pitfalls: The caller cannot supply trusted locks or a chosen digest.
Later alias changes cannot modify this publication; unavailable or revoked pinned artifacts must reject future admission rather than substitute another implementation.
operations.historicalInterpretation: Earlier PublishScenarioRevision becomes UpdateScenario followed by PublishScenario. Publication appends an ordinary Scenario version; there is no ScenarioRevision entity or mutable default pointer.

operations.purpose: Create an ARCHIVED Scenario head that blocks new run admissions while preserving prior publications.

useCase.title: Withdraw an exercise pending review
useCase.scenario: A scenario should no longer admit new executions until its assumptions are reviewed, but its past runs and publications must remain readable.
useCase.whenToUse: When intentionally withdrawing the whole Scenario from new admission.
steps: Read the current head and submit ArchiveScenario with its expectedVersion.
Inspect the archived result; review existing Runs separately if they need a cancellation decision.
useCase.intendedResult: All versions of this Scenario are blocked for new admissions while history and admitted runs remain intact.

preconditions: The caller needs archive authority and expectedVersion must match the current head.
pitfalls: Archiving does not cancel or redirect already admitted Runs.
Exact replay of a prior successful StartRun still returns its original receipt after reauthorization; archival must not change that admission history.
operations.historicalInterpretation: Earlier workflow archival was metadata on Scenario. The consolidated lifecycle records a new ARCHIVED representation under the common entity-version contract.

operations.purpose: Atomically admit one Run with an exact published program, exact subjects/bindings, StepRuns and a closed input Snapshot.

useCase.title: Execute a reviewed checkout exercise
useCase.scenario: An operator has chosen a published exercise and authorized test scope, and now wants one auditable execution intent.
useCase.whenToUse: When starting a new execution from an explicit PUBLISHED Scenario version.
steps: Select exact Scenario, subject and Connection versions, then provide inputs matching the pinned closed schema.
Submit a new clientToken for the new intent and inspect the returned Command, Run, Snapshot and StepRuns.
useCase.intendedResult: Admission fixes the program, input evidence, enabled steps and criterion denominator before dispatch.

preconditions: For a new admission, the current Scenario head must not be ARCHIVED; an intervening DRAFT does not replace the explicitly chosen publication. Subjects and bindings must satisfy current admission authority.
pitfalls: HTTP 200 and Run phase ADMITTED do not mean an AWS call has started.
Runtime skips or cancellation cannot shrink the admitted required-criterion denominator.
Retrying the same semantic request uses the same token; a genuinely new execution intent uses a new token.
operations.historicalInterpretation: The prior workflow admission contract retains immutable scope and program selection while scenarioRevisionId becomes an exact Scenario reference and connections use exact entity versions.

operations.purpose: Read a Run’s admitted references and independently qualified execution, assessment, effects and finalization state.

useCase.title: Explain a run whose workflow ended but cleanup remains uncertain
useCase.scenario: The main workflow has ended, yet an external effect has unresolved reconciliation. The reviewer needs more than one success flag.
useCase.whenToUse: When monitoring an admitted run or reading an exact historical representation.
steps: Read the current Run head for monitoring, or a cited version for historical review.
Inspect phase, executionOutcome, assessmentVerdict/finality, finalizationState and effectState separately; follow exact input and step references.
useCase.intendedResult: The run’s operational progress and workload conclusion remain independently explainable.

preconditions: The Run and its retained evidence closure must be currently authorized.
pitfalls: A successful HTTP read is not a successful run; successful execution is not automatically a passing workload criterion.
A later understanding belongs in new evidence or an evaluation projection and does not rewrite a sealed Run.
operations.historicalInterpretation: The earlier workflow Run projection is preserved while one ordinary Run.version replaces separate projection clocks.

operations.purpose: Locate retained workflow executions by exact Scenario reference or phase.

useCase.title: Find executions of a particular published exercise
useCase.scenario: A reviewer wants to compare runs that admitted the same program rather than mix runs from later scenario edits.
useCase.whenToUse: When locating run identities before inspecting their captured inputs and outcomes.
steps: Filter by the exact Scenario reference or phase as appropriate and traverse the fixed publication.
Open selected Runs and compare their exact admission evidence and independent result dimensions.
useCase.intendedResult: The reviewer can compare executions without losing the program version that each used.

preconditions: Scenario filters and returned Run closures must be authorized; the query must remain unchanged during pagination.
pitfalls: The list selects one head per Run identity within its traversal, not every historical Run version.
Shared Scenario identity alone does not prove identical program, subject, inputs or provider targets.
operations.historicalInterpretation: Earlier workflow run listing adopts RPC pagination and exact canonical references; it retains the distinction between separate executions and their read projections.

operations.purpose: Record monotonic cancellation intent under the current Run version and fence new main dispatch.

useCase.title: Cancel an exercise after an uncertain provider start
useCase.scenario: An exercise is no longer desired, but a provider start response was lost and the external effect may already exist.
useCase.whenToUse: When the operator intends to stop further main execution and enter bounded reconciliation/finalization.
steps: Read the Run head and submit the cancellation reason, expectedVersion and clientToken.
Inspect the returned Run/Command, then monitor effect reconciliation and finalization separately.
useCase.intendedResult: The first accepted cancellation intent becomes part of Run history without fabricating a remote stop result.

preconditions: expectedVersion must match after replay resolution. A new intent against a matching sealed Run returns accepted=false without changing it.
pitfalls: Cancellation does not declare provider effects stopped or workload recovery complete.
A creating Start must never be reissued after cancellation merely to discover a lost handle; unresolved effects retain their protection/hold.
A stale new intent conflicts; exact replay returns the original receipt before current-version checks.
operations.historicalInterpretation: The earlier workflow cancellation semantics are retained under RPC with one Run.version; cleanup, assessment verdict and execution outcome remain distinct.

operations.purpose: Read a Run-owned step representation with its phase, outcome, selected attempt and exact attempt history.

useCase.title: Explain why a required criterion was skipped
useCase.scenario: A run contains a criterion step with zero attempts because its dependency did not permit dispatch. The reviewer must see the explicit skip.
useCase.whenToUse: When inspecting one compiled step or following an exact reference from Run.steps.
steps: Use runId, stepRunId and the version referenced by the chosen Run representation.
Inspect skipReason, phase, outcome and selectedAttempt before reading attempt evidence.
useCase.intendedResult: The reviewer can distinguish an unattempted step from a failed attempt or a completed criterion.

preconditions: The StepRun must belong to the supplied Run; exact referenced versions must be available.
pitfalls: The selected attempt is explicit and is not inferred from the largest attemptNo.
Read access does not imply a public step-status, retry or stop writer exists.

operations.purpose: Resolve the exact step set retained by a selected Run version.

useCase.title: Reconstruct the step view of a past Run representation
useCase.scenario: The Run head has advanced since an incident review. The reviewer needs the StepRun versions that belonged to the earlier Run state.
useCase.whenToUse: When displaying or auditing a Run’s immutable step selection.
steps: Pass runId and the chosen runVersion; omission deliberately selects the Run head once.
Follow returned exact StepRun versions in retained compiled order, including skipped zero-attempt steps.
useCase.intendedResult: The parent’s historical step view cannot acquire later child state.

preconditions: Current authorization applies to the selected Run and each referenced child; missing exact child versions fail the read.
pitfalls: The operation must not join to current StepRun heads or reconstruct children by timestamp.
Pagination binds the selected parent and its immutable member set, not a moving live view.
operations.historicalInterpretation: The earlier ListRunSteps preserves all compiled steps, while v2 makes parent selection and exact child-version references explicit.

operations.purpose: Read the execution facts and evidence for one attempt under its Run and StepRun ownership.

useCase.title: Review an uncertain native operation attempt
useCase.scenario: A fault-injection step dispatched a native operation but could not establish its result. The analyst needs the exact attempt facts and external-operation evidence.
useCase.whenToUse: When inspecting why a step selected an attempt or why an effect remains unresolved.
steps: Supply the complete parent chain and exact StepAttempt version referenced by the StepRun.
Inspect outcome, checkResult, externalOperations and evidenceRefs without inventing a later success.
useCase.intendedResult: The attempt’s recorded execution facts remain independently reviewable.

preconditions: The attempt must belong to the given StepRun and Run, and its evidence must be authorized.
pitfalls: attemptNo is a retry ordinal, not the entity version.
A settled attempt does not reopen; late reconciliation adds evidence rather than rewriting sealed facts.

operations.purpose: Resolve the exact attempt history retained by a selected StepRun version, ordered by attemptNo.

useCase.title: Audit whether a retry was justified
useCase.scenario: A step has several recorded attempts. The reviewer needs to understand which attempts existed at a chosen step state and which one was selected.
useCase.whenToUse: When examining retry history or a step’s exact execution evidence.
steps: Pass runId, stepRunId and the desired stepRunVersion.
Read the exact attempts returned in attemptNo order and compare the selectedAttempt on that same StepRun.
useCase.intendedResult: The retry history stays consistent with the selected parent representation.

preconditions: The supplied StepRun must belong to the Run; exact referenced attempt versions must be authorized and available.
pitfalls: Polling, resume and transport retry remain within the same attempt; they do not automatically justify another attempt.
A new mutating attempt is forbidden while its predecessor’s effect is unresolved.
This read operation offers no independent retry or attempt-status command.
operations.historicalInterpretation: The earlier attempt listing retains its ascending attempt number and execution facts, with v2 pinning exact children through an ordinary StepRun version.

operations.purpose: Read a native FIS experiment independently from any application workflow Run.

useCase.title: Inspect what a fault experiment actually affected
useCase.scenario: A workflow links a native experiment. The operator needs its native state, named action states, selected targets, effect evidence and report readiness.
useCase.whenToUse: When following an external-operation link or reviewing an imported experiment.
steps: Read the exact Experiment version referenced by evidence, or its current head for monitoring.
Inspect named actions, target memberships, resolution coverage and report facts separately from the workflow’s assessment verdict.
useCase.intendedResult: The native experiment can be understood on its own terms while retaining any verified workflow relationship.

preconditions: The experiment and retained observation must be authorized within its provider scope.
pitfalls: An action’s catalog actionId identifies an action type; execution identity is experiment plus actionName.
Selected targets, applied effects, workload criteria and report completion are separate evidence dimensions.

operations.purpose: Discover retained FIS experiments by observing connection or verified workflow linkage.

useCase.title: Find the experiment associated with an exercise
useCase.scenario: A Run may have a reconciled native experiment, and the operator wants to locate that experiment without confusing it with unrelated imported experiments.
useCase.whenToUse: When navigating native experiments after provider evidence has been retained.
steps: Use connectionId or runId filters as appropriate.
Inspect each returned experiment and verify the retained external-operation link before attributing it to the workflow.
useCase.intendedResult: Native experiments remain discoverable whether or not they were created by a product Run.

preconditions: The caller must have current experiment-read authority and the run filter must use verified ExternalOperationRef links.
pitfalls: An imported experiment can validly have no Run.
A similar name, template or timestamp does not prove workflow membership.

operations.purpose: Admit a provider request to stop one whole native FIS experiment.

useCase.title: Stop a fault experiment whose effects need reconciliation
useCase.scenario: The operator has verified the target experiment and wants the native stop request tracked separately from its final state and cleanup.
useCase.whenToUse: When intentionally requesting a whole-experiment stop through an authorized connection.
steps: Read the Experiment head and its suitable exact Source precondition.
Submit expectedVersion, expectedSource and an exact Connection with the stop intent, then follow the Command and experiment observations.
useCase.intendedResult: The stop request has a durable receipt while final native state and recovery are established through evidence.

preconditions: The source must belong to the same native experiment; connection scope and current dispatch authority must be valid.
pitfalls: Stop acceptance does not prove final state, post-action cleanup, workload recovery or report completion.
No individual native action stop, pause or retry API is invented.
This request does not replace Run cancellation; workflow intent and native effect handling remain separately explicit.
